Subject: Question on SLA uptime floor and monthly credits

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the draft SLA earlier. A couple of items came up from our ops and procurement teams:

- The template's standard uptime floor is 99.95% for hosted plans — our ops lead expects a justification for that versus 99.9% for our workload patterns (bursting batch inference). Can you share any client precedent or risk assessment?
- On monthly remedy credits: the draft shows a stepped credit schedule but doesn't call out a monthly cap. Procurement needs a clear maximum liability (their legal asks for a percent-of-invoice cap).
- We also want to confirm how scheduled maintenance windows are treated — specifically if planned maintenance for model updates will reduce the uptime calculation.

Can you propose an adjusted template (or point us to the recommended variant) that addresses those three points so we can run it through our legal? Happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Director, Infrastructure
HelioWorks

Subject: Re: Question on SLA uptime floor and monthly credits

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I attach a marked-up template: helioworks_sla_draft_v2.pdf.

1) Uptime floor: we recommend 99.95% for our hosted tier when the customer uses a reserved or dedicated capacity profile (predictable capacity + isolation). For fully shared, bursty public pools, 99.9% is the baseline we historically offer. For HelioWorks' use case (steady scheduled batches + latency-sensitive API paths), the slightly higher floor reduces tail exposure during contention. I included a short precedent table in redwood_sla_summary.xlsx.

2) Monthly cap: we've proposed a 6%-of-monthly-invoice cap in the draft. That balances customer protection with our risk (we've seen requests cap at 5–10% historically). If procurement prefers a hard dollar cap instead, we can map that from an estimated monthly run-rate.

3) Scheduled maintenance: the draft treats planned maintenance windows (72+ hours notice) as carveouts from uptime only if scheduled in the monthly maintenance calendar and if they do not exceed X hours/month (we proposed 6 hours/month). For model updates that require rolling restarts, those are listed as "operational maintenance" and excluded from uptime if pre-notified; emergency patches are not excluded.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura: legal review of the 6% cap and the maintenance carveouts (redlines in the attached PDF).
- Ben: ops/product confirmation on the 6 hours/month breakpoint and the recommended language for rolling updates.

If HelioWorks is open, I'd like to schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the marked-up template together and capture any redlines in real time.

Thanks,
Marissa

Laura / Ben — forwarding the note from HelioWorks. Key asks: justification for 99.95% vs 99.9%, explicit monthly cap, and clarity on scheduled maintenance carveouts for model updates.

My suggested compromise (see attached):
- Offer 99.95% uptime for Dedicated/Reserved plan; keep 99.9% for Shared/On-demand. Call this out in the "Service Levels" table with clear mapping to plan types.
- Set monthly remedy cap to 6% of invoice by default; allow negotiation to a fixed-dollar cap where customers provide committed spend.
- Scheduled maintenance: carve out pre-notified windows (>=72 hours notice) up to 6 hours/month. Rolling model updates that require brief node restarts are permitted under that 6-hour bucket if we provide the maintenance calendar.

Questions for you:
- Laura: is 6% an acceptable default for sale without additional legal approval? If not, what language tweaks make it palatable (e.g., exclude third-party infra outages)?
- Ben: product/ops: can we consistently keep rolling update windows under 6 hours/month for HelioWorks' expected cadence? If not, suggest an operational SLA alternative (e.g., scheduled model-update blackout periods).

I indicated I'm happy to do a joint call with Alicia tomorrow morning.

—Marissa

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear questions and for flagging procurement's preference. We reviewed Marissa's marked-up template and Ben's input about operational windows. Summary of agreed changes below; I've also attached a clean PDF for signature.

1) Uptime floor:
- We will offer 99.95% for HelioWorks on the Dedicated plan (language updated to map plan type to service level). For Shared/on-demand we will retain 99.9%. This gives HelioWorks the higher SLA tied to reserved capacity.

2) Monthly remedy cap:
- Default remedial liability capped at 6% of the monthly invoice, per Marissa's draft.
- We added a clause allowing substitution with a fixed-dollar cap when the customer provides a committed monthly spend figure (section 4.3).

3) Scheduled maintenance & model updates: 
- Planned maintenance (>=72 hours notice) is carved out from uptime up to 6 hours/month.
- Rolling model updates that require short restarts will be scheduled into the maintenance calendar and count toward the 6 hours. Emergency fixes are excluded from carveouts.

4) Additional clarifications/legal protections:
- Excluded causes expanded to include third-party cloud provider catastrophic events (we will not accept third-party infrastructure as our liability in those cases).
- Remedy calculation examples added to Annex A to avoid ambiguity during bill reconciliation.

If HelioWorks is comfortable with these edits, we'll send the clean PDF and a DocuSign link (DocuSign link will appear in the HubSpot record). If you want a different cap, let us know the target and we'll run a counterpart redline.

Thanks — happy to join a short call this afternoon if you'd like to walk the changes.

Laura Bennett
